extracted.intended_audience: scientists, engineers, science communicators, science advocates, and organizations involved in public engagement
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for designing and evaluating public engagement activities that create intentional, meaningful, two-way interactions between scientists and the public, with goals such as civic empowerment and recognition of multiple perspectives. Focuses on purpose, mutual learning, desired outcomes, and topical scope (research, education, policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Public engagement with science describes intentional, meaningful interactions that provide opportunities for mutual learning between scientists and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition as the baseline standard for what counts as public engagement activities (i.e., they should be purposeful and enable two-way exchange rather than one-way transmission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentionality and meaningfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement should be intentional and meaningful rather than incidental or purely promotional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities with explicit objectives for interaction and relevance to participants, avoiding token outreach or one-off events that do not foster substantive exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual learning (bidirectional exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutual learning refers not just to the acquisition of knowledge, but also to increased familiarity with a breadth of perspectives, frames, and worldviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate engagement by whether both scientists and public participants gain understanding — scientific content and diverse perspectives alike — rather than treating the public solely as recipients of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic engagement skills and empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals for public engagement with science include civic engagement skills and empowerment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether activities build participants' capacity to act in civic contexts (e.g., informed decision-making, advocacy, participation in policy processes) and whether they increase participants' sense of agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural relevance awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: increased awareness of the cultural relevance of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether engagement connects scientific topics to participants' cultural contexts and values, making science more relevant and accessible to diverse communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of multiple perspectives and knowledge domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: recognition of the importance of multiple perspectives and domains of knowledge to scientific endeavors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate if engagement acknowledges and incorporates non-scientific knowledge systems, community expertise, and varied worldviews into dialogue about science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and institutional scope for engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAS engages the public and empowers scientists to engage the public on issues related to research, education, policy, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning or assessing engagement, ensure activities are linked to relevant topical domains (research findings, education initiatives, policy discussions) and consider institutional roles in supporting sustained engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of toolkits and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAS provides resources such as the 'Take Action Toolkit' and 'AAAS Communication Toolkit' to support public engagement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage established toolkits and organizational resources to design, implement, and evaluate engagement efforts; these resources may contain practical steps, templates, and further standards.
